components.name: Recording Mic
components.description: The signature 80px circular magenta-gradient mic button with concentric pulsing rings. The emotional center of the app.
components.css: .ds-mic-wrap { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 180px; height: 180px; } .ds-mic { width: 80px; height: 80px; border-radius: 50%; border: none; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #E50074, #B8005E); box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(229,0,116,0.40); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; z-index: 1; transition: box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 150ms; } .ds-mic:hover { box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(229,0,116,0.50); } .ds-mic:active { transform: scale(0.95); } .ds-mic-ring { position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid rgba(229,0,116,0.15); animation: ds-mic-pulse 3.5s ease-in-out infinite; pointer-events: none; } .ds-mic-ring.r1 { width: 120px; height: 120px; } .ds-mic-ring.r2 { width: 150px; height: 150px; animation-delay: 0.8s; } @keyframes ds-mic-pulse { 0% { opacity: 0.4; transform: scale(0.9); } 50% { opacity: 0.15; transform: scale(1.0); } 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1.15); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-mic-ring { animation: none; opacity: 0.2; } }

narrative.overview: TranscriptStudio is a branded workspace, not a neutral utility. It is unmistakably Yinga the moment it loads: the four-color spinner, the magenta wordmark, magenta gradients on every primary action. But it earns that brand confidence by sitting inside a calm, Apple-native shell. The single most important fact about this system is that it is one design language rendered twice: the macOS/iOS app and the Windows app carry identical hex values, spacing, radii, and animation curves. The aesthetic is warm-friendly-professional and explicitly rejects the generic dark-mode SaaS dashboard look; depth comes from translucency and soft shadow, never heavy chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Cross-platform parity is law — every token exists identically in Color+Brand.swift/Theme.swift and globals.css.
Yinga magenta #E50074 leads every primary action, usually as a 135 degree gradient into #B8005E.
Glass surfaces (backdrop-filter blur 20px, translucent fill) carry the entire card system on both platforms.
SF Pro Rounded for headings/titles gives the friendly voice; system sans for body keeps it legible.
8pt spacing grid, continuous-corner radii, spring/ease-out motion — Apple HIG rhythm throughout.
Full light + dark adaptive palettes, both first-class.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Magenta acts, blue navigates. Primary actions and recording are magenta; selection, tabs, links, and focus-within-navigation are blue. Never use magenta for a nav-selection state or blue for a primary CTA.

rules.name: The Parity Rule
rules.body: No color or token exists on one platform only. Every value lives identically in Color+Brand.swift and globals.css. A new value is added to both or it does not exist.

rules.name: The Rounded-Heading Rule
rules.body: Anything title-tier and up uses the rounded design (.rounded on macOS, SF Pro Rounded on web). Body and controls use plain system sans.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Label-Only Rule
rules.body: Uppercase + tracked is reserved for <=2-word labels and badges at the 10px micro size. Never uppercase a sentence or a button.

rules.name: The Glass-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, flyouts, badges, and the sidebar are glass over the canvas. Solid opaque panels are the exception. Dark mode deepens shadows, it does not remove the glass.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Hover Rule
rules.body: Interactive surfaces respond to hover with a ~1.02 scale + shadow bump + accent border tint on a 180ms ease. Use .card-static only where lift is wrong.

dos: Do keep every token identical across Color+Brand.swift/Theme.swift and globals.css — parity is the system.
Do use magenta #E50074 for actions and the mic, blue #007BC4 for navigation/selection/focus.
Do render primary buttons and the mic as the 135 degree magenta gradient with the colored glow shadow.
Do build surfaces as glass over the gray canvas, with 1px translucent borders and soft ambient shadow.
Do use SF Pro Rounded for titles and headlines; plain system sans for body and controls.
Do stay on the 8pt spacing grid and the 6/12/16/20/25px radius ladder.
Do give interactive surfaces a ~1.02 hover lift + shadow + accent-border tint, with a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
Do support light and dark equally; both palettes are first-class.
donts: Don't let this drift into a generic dark-mode SaaS dashboard (neon-on-charcoal, sharp corners, dense grids).
Don't use a border-left/border-right colored stripe as a card or callout accent (the web hero-CTA left-border is legacy, not a pattern).
Don't introduce gradient text (background-clip: text); gradients belong on fills and buttons only.
Don't add flat opaque panels where a glass card belongs, or convey depth with heavy/dark drop shadows.
Don't set body or button copy in UPPERCASE — uppercase is the 10px tracked label/badge size only.
Don't swap the action/navigation colors (magenta nav-selection or blue primary CTA).
Don't add a color, radius, or spacing value to one platform without adding the identical value to the other.
Don't introduce a third display typeface; the rounded + system-sans pairing is the whole type system.
